name: Gummy smile Botox

image.caption: After Botox and fillers to reduce gummy smile

lead: Gummy smile Botox is used by people who want less gum showing when they smile. Small amounts of botulinum toxin go into the muscles that lift the upper lip, so the lip rises less and the teeth take up more of the smile.

The toxin blocks nerve signals to those muscles, which lowers the lip line within days. Many small registered trials have compared injection sites and doses, guidance methods and combinations with surgery. Wikipedia reports an average duration of roughly six months.

paras: It is a clinic treatment given by a trained clinician, usually a short visit. The lowered lip line appears within days, and people repeat it when the effect fades. Some combine it with gum or lip surgery when the gum line is also part of the cause. Gummy smile is generally an off-label use.

Described effects include weakness of nearby muscles, bruising and headache, and the smile can look different while the toxin is active. It is a prescription product administered by clinicians, and the result wears off, so it is temporary.

angle.text: Botulinum toxin in the upper lip muscles is used by people who want less gum showing when they smile. The lip rises less, and the lowered lip line is visible within days. The result is temporary, and many small trials have measured it.

lead: Botulinum toxin treatment for a gummy smile involves injecting the toxin into the muscles that lift the upper lip so the lip rises less on smiling and less gum shows.[1][2] A gummy smile, or excessive gingival display, is commonly described as more than about 2 mm of gum visible above the upper front teeth when smiling.[1]

Wikipedia describes the effect as lasting an average of about six months, and botulinum toxin cosmetic effects in general are temporary and require repeat treatment.[1][2] Registered trials have compared injection sites and doses, EMG guidance, and combinations with surgery, though many are small.[3][4][5]
infobox: Prescription-only product; gummy smile use is generally off-label

paras: Injections are placed in the upper lip elevator muscles, such as levator labii superioris, levator labii superioris alaeque nasi and zygomaticus minor.[1] The toxin blocks release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, relaxing the muscle.[2] Some studies describe a specific site called the Yonsei point.[6]

Wikipedia reports an average duration of about six months, citing a 2018 systematic review.[1] Trials registered on the topic have studied dose and site,[7][7] higher doses,[8] and zinc supplementation.[9] A 2022 analysis of YouTube videos on Botox for gummy smile evaluated their content quality and accuracy.[10]

General cosmetic botulinum toxin effects described include unintended weakness of nearby muscles, bruising and headache.[2] A registered study is examining decision regret after Yonsei-point injection.[11]

Registered human studies include a trial of injection dose and site (n=55),[7] a higher-dose phase 1/2 trial (n=33),[8] a study of the Yonsei point (n=48),[6] EMG-guided versus conventional injection (n=32),[3] a comparison with crown lengthening surgery (n=20),[5] a satisfaction study of adults (n=22),[12] and a planned comparison with hyaluronic acid filler.[13] One trial was withdrawn.[4] Results are not summarised here where not published in the sources used.
The procedure is considered a temporary, non-surgical counterpart to lip repositioning and gum surgery for gummy smiles.[1]
